solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fool cancelled radical playwright

parts.note: a berk is a fool (British slang)
a match that is off has been cancelled

explanation.surface: A radical playwright is dismissed as a fool whose show has been cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Steven Berkoff is the British actor-playwright known for his confrontational, physical theatre. BERK is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Berkoff's stylised, aggressive plays made him the radical of the British stage.

clue.text: Raccoon's been shot south of British national park

indicators.note: something shot is ruined, so the letters come out wrecked and rearranged
in a down clue, south of a letter means written below it

parts.note: B = British
the twelve letters of RACCOONS BEEN rearranged

explanation.surface: A hunter reports that a raccoon has been shot somewhere south of a British national park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as gunfire but means the letters are wrecked. The Brecon Beacons are mountains in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beacons in south Wales were designated one of Britain's national parks in 1957.

clue.text: Intend to wear ripped clothing

indicators.note: a word that wears another has it on, wrapped around it like a coat

parts.note: rent = torn, ripped
to aim is to intend

explanation.surface: Someone means to go out in torn clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts 'to wear' and 'clothing' side by side so the whole clue seems to be about dressing; only 'clothing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An old, literary word for garments, found mostly in the Bible and poetry.

clue.text: Group table depleted in a month

indicators.note: a depleted word has had its contents used up, leaving only its shell

parts.note: OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October

indicators.note: the emptied table sits inside the month

parts.note: TABLE emptied of its middle leaves T…E

explanation.surface: A group finds the table empty during a certain month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depleted' means the word loses all its contents, not just a letter or two; only the outer letters of TABLE survive.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of eight performers or things is one kind of group.

clue.text: At first, factoids and numbers suit organised admirers

indicators.note: taking each word at its first means reading only its opening letter

parts.note: the first letters of Factoids And Numbers
clubs is one of the four card suits

explanation.surface: Trivia and statistics appeal to an organised body of enthusiasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' reads as a verb, as in 'factoids suit admirers', but it is the noun: a suit of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirers of a star who form a society with membership and newsletters are organised.

clue.text: Court order briefly introduced to silence chatterbox

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short and loses its last letter
something introduced to a thing is put into it

parts.note: to gag is to silence
ASBO, an anti-social behaviour order, cut short

explanation.surface: A judge issues a court order to shut up someone who talks too much.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British court order restraining nuisance behaviour. The surface makes the order the thing that silences; in the wordplay it is the part slipped inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for someone who talks too much, the first suggesting hot air.

clue.text: Male races in run for lowly quarter?

indicators.note: the man and the races go inside the word for run

parts.note: to go is to run, as a machine does
he = a male
the TT races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man runs races in search of a cheap part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle race meeting, a crossword staple for 'races'.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor, segregated district of a city is a quarter of low standing.

clue.text: Hairy beast crouching in small out-of-bounds dacha

indicators.note: a word put out of its bounds loses its boundary letters, first and last

parts.note: S = small

indicators.note: the crouching word goes inside what is left of the dacha

parts.note: DACHA with its bounds (first and last letters) removed
to squat is to crouch

explanation.surface: A hairy beast crouches inside a little Russian country house it should not be in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out-of-bounds' reads as forbidden, but it strips the boundary letters from DACHA. A dacha is a Russian country cottage.
explanation.definitionFit: Also called Bigfoot, the ape-man of North American legend is covered in hair.

clue.text: French city soon collects six grand

indicators.note: a word that collects others gathers them up and holds them inside

parts.note: anon = soon, in old usage
VI = six in Roman numerals
G = grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A French city will soon receive six thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' reads as an adjective describing the city, but it is slang for a thousand, abbreviated G.
explanation.definitionFit: The Provençal city on the Rhône was the seat of the popes in the 14th century.

clue.text: Being sixteen, boisterous and extremely carefree

indicators.note: boisterous means rowdy and unruly, so the letters will not stay in line
taken at its extremes, a word gives only its first and last letters

parts.note: anagram fodder
the extreme letters of CarefreE

explanation.surface: A portrait of being a rowdy, carefree sixteen-year-old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like the start of a sentence about a teenager; it is the definition, as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, being is the plain synonym: the state of being alive or real.

clue.text: Superficially deals with captains

definitions.meaning: to skip a topic is to pass over it lightly
skip = skipper, the captain of a team or boat

explanation.surface: Someone treats their leaders with only surface attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captains' reads as a noun being dealt with; it is a second definition in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means passing lightly over a subject; the noun is short for skippers, team captains in curling and bowls.

clue.text: Selected MPs secretly follow case surrounding TV

parts.note: to shadow someone is to tail them unseen
the wooden cabinet that old television sets were built into

explanation.surface: Chosen MPs are being tailed, perhaps by someone watching a TV case.
explanation.walkthrough: The shadow cabinet is the team of opposition MPs who each mirror a government minister; the leader selects them.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposition leader picks a team of MPs to mirror the ministers, so they are selected.

clue.text: Public secret initially suppressed

indicators.note: a word whose initial is suppressed has its first letter held back

parts.note: covert = secret

explanation.surface: A secret that was stifled at first has come into public view.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the word being trimmed are opposites, which is the pleasure of the clue: one letter turns a secret into its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Done openly rather than hidden, so public, a plain synonym.

clue.text: First couple from Hungary trapped in rioting Italian republic

indicators.note: the first couple of letters from a word are its first two
rioting means running wild, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: ITALIAN rearranged

indicators.note: the two letters are caught inside the rearranged word

parts.note: the first two letters of HUngary

explanation.surface: Two Hungarians are caught up in an Italian riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian republic' reads as one phrase, but 'Italian' belongs to the wordplay and 'republic' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic state has been an independent republic since 1990, a definition by example.

clue.text: Die in hot water?

parts.note: not the verb for dying but the noun: a die is a cube
not in trouble but literally in a hot bath

explanation.surface: Someone meets their end in trouble, or in scalding water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Die' reads as a verb about death; it is the noun, a dice cube. A bath cube is a scented block that dissolves in bathwater.
explanation.definitionFit: A scented block of bath salts is cube-shaped like a die and is dropped into a hot bath.

clue.text: Old county Conservative getting even afterwards

parts.note: C = Conservative
level = even
and = and then, afterwards, as in 'he ate and left'

explanation.surface: A Tory in an old county finally settles the score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting even' reads as revenge, but 'even' alone is LEVEL, and 'getting' only joins it to the Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: The county around Middlesbrough existed only from 1974 to 1996, so it is an old one.

clue.text: Drunken idiots rolling over floor

indicators.note: something rolling over turns upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: nits = idiots
to floor someone is to knock them out, KO

explanation.surface: Drunk fools are tumbling about on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is exactly the scene of the answer, drunks on the floor, and 'floor' is a verb in the wordplay: to knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang synonym for very drunk.

clue.text: Jockey announced "great success" after losing round in sporting event

indicators.note: round is the letter O, the shape of a circle, and it is lost
something announced is spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the jockey

parts.note: a jockey is a rider; the name is spelt differently
COUP, a great success, without the letter O

explanation.surface: A jockey declares a triumph at a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ryder Cup is the golf contest between Europe and the USA. 'Round' is the letter O, shaped like a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The biennial Europe-versus-USA golf tournament is a sporting event, a definition by example.

clue.text: Flier takes part in viva voce tests

indicators.note: the answer is a part taken from inside the following words

parts.note: vivA VOCE Tests

explanation.surface: An aviator sits oral examinations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a pilot sitting exams; it is a bird. The avocet is a wading bird with an upturned bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A black-and-white wading bird, so a flier by example; a viva voce is an oral exam.

clue.text: Public company starts to manufacture excellent product

parts.note: once news is out, it is public
CO = company

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their first letters

parts.note: the first letters of Manufacture and Excellent

explanation.surface: A listed company begins making a first-rate product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Public company' reads as one business term from the stock market, and 'product' as goods off a line; both split apart here.
explanation.definitionFit: A product in the sense of a result, what something yields.

clue.text: Snake-like, unusually hypnotic

indicators.note: done unusually, the letters are not in their usual order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Something snake-like and strangely mesmerising, like Kaa in The Jungle Book.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits the answer: snakes are famed for hypnotising their prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Formed from the name of a big constrictor, it means resembling that snake.

clue.text: Report of bad general situation for molluscs

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the answer sounds like the phrase

parts.note: naughty = bad, and the lie of the land is the general situation

explanation.surface: A news report describes a bad situation for shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' here is the lie of the land, the general layout of things. The plural is Latin, with -I.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiral-shelled sea creatures related to squid are cephalopod molluscs.

clue.text: Radio astronomer's source of celestial observations early in year?

parts.note: January comes early in the year
the sky is where stars are observed

explanation.surface: A radio astronomer's January sky watching.
explanation.walkthrough: Karl Jansky was the American engineer who founded radio astronomy; the unit of radio flux is named after him. The clue half-says 'Jan's sky'.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Jansky first detected radio waves from the Milky Way in the 1930s.

clue.text: Goethe upset with man working as a solicitor?

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so its letters fall out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The German poet is annoyed with a man who works as a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests an English lawyer, but here it is someone soliciting in the street. The answer is British slang for working as a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A prostitute solicits for clients, so the question mark flags a solicitor of an unlegal sort.

clue.text: Uncovered disparagements in, say, King's promotional description

indicators.note: a word uncovered has its covering stripped off, its first and last letters

parts.note: B.B. King, the blues guitarist; 'say' marks him as one example of a King

indicators.note: the stripped word goes inside the king's initials

parts.note: SLURS with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: Insults about a monarch are exposed in some advertising copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King' looks like royalty; it is the bluesman B.B. King. 'Uncovered' strips the covering letters from SLURS.
explanation.definitionFit: The short puff on a book jacket is a promotional description.

clue.text: One way to join equid when cycling

indicators.note: letters cycling go round like a wheel, the front ones coming round to the back

parts.note: the zebra is a member of the horse family, Equidae

explanation.surface: A way to link up with a horse while out on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' reads as riding a bicycle; it means letters wheeling round from one end to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldering metal with a brass alloy is one method of joining.

clue.text: Car manufacturer endorses backing Russian agreement

indicators.note: backing a word runs it in reverse, like a car

parts.note: to OK something is to endorse it
da = yes in Russian

explanation.surface: A carmaker supports a deal with Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as supporting, which is what 'endorses' already means; here it turns the endorsement round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Czech carmaker, now part of Volkswagen, is a definition by example.

clue.text: Narrow-minded Jack stops fighting in case

indicators.note: letters fighting are thrown about in a scuffle
the sailor stops a gap, plugging himself into the middle of the other letters

parts.note: IN CASE rearranged
a jack tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A bigoted man called Jack breaks up a fight, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In case' reads as a phrase meaning 'as a precaution', but it is six letters of fodder. Jack and TAR both mean a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigoted in favour of one's own sect or faction, hence narrow-minded.

clue.text: Bloom's colour about to be hidden by grass

indicators.note: about means turned round, as in about-face

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: a word hidden by another is tucked away inside it

parts.note: to colour is to dye

explanation.surface: A flower's colour is about to vanish in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloom' looks like a flower, and 'about to' like 'soon going to'; 'about' alone is the reversal, and 'Bloom' is the prime of life.
explanation.definitionFit: In full bloom means at one's peak, and the answer is that prime time.

clue.text: Foretell old Brit will consume wine

indicators.note: the old Brit drinks the wine down, so it ends up inside him

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of Scotland
red = red wine

explanation.surface: A prophecy that an ancient Briton will drink some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: PICT for 'old Brit' is a crossword regular: the Picts lived in what is now Scotland before the Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to say what will happen before it does.
